title: Rightward cascade preserves side words
statement: For a natural number $\ell$, let $C_i=2\cdot 2^i$ be the capacity of zone $i$, and let $z$ be a configuration of a home value and left and right lists at each index $i<\ell$, with each list having length at most $C_i$. Let $j<\ell$. Suppose the right lists at all indices $k<j$ are empty, the left list at each such index has length $C_k$, the right list at index $j$ is nonempty, and the left list at index $j$ has length at most $C_j-2^{j-1}$. After the rightward cascade through zone $j$, the concatenation of the left lists is the home value prepended to its original concatenation, and the concatenation of the right lists is the tail of its original concatenation.
hypotheses_covered: Each left and right list in $z$ has length at most its zone capacity
Right lists at indices $k<j$ are empty
Left lists at indices $k<j$ have length equal to their zone capacities
The right list at index $j$ is nonempty
The left list at index $j$ has length plus $2^{j-1}$ at most its capacity
